comment: Advisories that match a dependency's version but are accepted - see docs/dependencies.md. status: unreachable (the vulnerable code is never used), mitigated (closed in ws-client's own code), residual (NOT closed - documented, with the way out). An entry covers exactly its artifact, versions and ids.

accepted.reason: The Brotli, Bzip2, LZ4 and Snappy decoders are never in the pipeline: only gzip and deflate response bodies are decoded (Netty's zlib decoders).
These Netty versions decode only gzip and deflate response bodies (they have no Brotli, Zstandard or Snappy content decoder), and the engine bounds the decompressed size itself.
Needs pipelined requests with a `HEAD` among them: AsyncHttpClient sends one request at a time per connection, and the engine sends no `HEAD`.

No caller-supplied value reaches the request line or a header with a raw line break: query keys and values are percent-encoded, and a URL or header with a line break is refused or encoded before Netty sees it - pinned on every engine by `TestServers.lineBreakInjection`. Netty's `HttpPostRequestEncoder` is not used (multipart bodies are built by ws-client).

Lenient parsing of chunk sizes, chunk extensions, `Transfer-Encoding` and control characters: request smuggling against a server or proxy that parses REQUESTS with Netty. The engine parses responses only, on connections pooled per target host - the one peer that can send such a response is the site itself.
Server-side code - the multipart request decoder, the CORS handler, the response encoder, WebSocket handshakers, SPDY: a client pipeline has none of it.
Server-side code - the multipart request decoder, the CORS handler, the response encoder, WebSocket handshakers, SPDY: a client pipeline has none of it.

NOT closed. Windows only, local attacker: at start-up Netty reads `C:\etc\os-release`, which a local user may create - a huge one exhausts the JVM's memory. It matters on a Windows host shared with untrusted local users. No Play WS release for Akka on Scala 2.12 or Scala 3 carries a fixed Netty: there, use Scala 2.13 (Play WS 2.2.18) or the Pekko flavor.
Server-side handlers (`SniHandler`, `IpSubnetFilter`).

Needs a caller-supplied plain `X509TrustManager`: the engine supplies none - certificates and host names are checked by the JDK's default trust managers. Pinned by the Play provider specs (an untrusted certificate and a certificate for another host name are rejected).

Reached by gzip and deflate response bodies. The engine's bounded inflater fails a response whose decompressed size passes its limit (256 MiB by default); what stays unbounded by it is the inflation of ONE network read (at most about a thousand times a 64 KiB read buffer) before the limit is checked.
Netty's `HttpProxyHandler` is not used: AsyncHttpClient opens `CONNECT` tunnels itself, and the engine configures no SOCKS proxy.

Closed in ws-client: where the bundled AsyncHttpClient has no limit, the engine replaces its response inflater with a bounded one (`maxDecompressedResponseSize`, 256 MiB by default). Pinned by the Play provider specs with a gzip bomb.
The engine runs AsyncHttpClient without a cookie store (`setCookieStore(null)`): no cookie is stored or replayed. Pinned on every engine by `TestServers.cookieIsolation`.
The engine runs AsyncHttpClient without a cookie store (`setCookieStore(null)`): no cookie is stored or replayed. Pinned on every engine by `TestServers.cookieIsolation`.

Needs AsyncHttpClient's own logins (a `Realm`: Basic, Digest, NTLM, Kerberos) or proxy credentials: the engine configures neither. A site's credentials are plain request headers, and they never go on the `CONNECT` to a proxy (pinned by `TestServers.connectRequestHead`).

Needs AsyncHttpClient's own logins (a `Realm`: Basic, Digest, NTLM, Kerberos) or proxy credentials: the engine configures neither. A site's credentials are plain request headers, and they never go on the `CONNECT` to a proxy (pinned by `TestServers.connectRequestHead`).
Redirects are never followed (`setFollowRedirect(false)`, whatever the JVM-wide AsyncHttpClient property says). Pinned by the Play provider specs.

A replay to another host needs a `ResponseFilter` that returns a different request, or a followed redirect: the engine installs no filter and follows no redirect. AsyncHttpClient's own I/O retry replays to the same host, which is not affected.
The engine opens no WebSocket.
The engine opens no WebSocket.

Denial of service while PARSING protobuf input. Akka (which shades this protobuf-java in `akka-protobuf-v3`) parses protobuf only when it deserializes messages from another node - remoting, cluster, persistence, stream refs. The engines' actor systems are local: none of those Akka modules is a dependency (this page's lists show it), so no protobuf input is ever parsed. Akka 2.6.21 is the last Akka 2.6 release; the Pekko flavor's protobuf-java (4.33.5) is not affected.
